indexes.name: document_embeddings_vector_index
indexes.note: v1, live since MONEY-613. B0 §7 read it back as type=vectorSearch, dims=768, similarity=cosine, quantization=absent. Its FILTER fields were not printed by that run, so they are declared here as the set the readers actually send (apps/web/lib/gemini/vector-store.ts filters on userId AND docType) — if the live index turns out to declare fewer, --verify prints the difference rather than correcting it.

indexes.name: document_embeddings_v2_vector_index
indexes.note: v2. Same dims and the SAME similarity as v1 — the vendor's own supported-similarity table allows cosine for binData(int8) (euclidean-only is the int1 rule), so B0 §5's open gate closes without a normalization pass or a move to dotProduct. `quantization` is ABSENT on purpose: automatic quantization over an already-quantized field makes Atlas skip every vector.

indexes.name: document_embeddings_v2_probe_index
indexes.note: The canary. One synthetic row, so `--probe` can prove that (1) Prisma's $runCommandRaw carries an extended-JSON binary of subtype 9 into Mongo intact and (2) Atlas accepts a BinData queryVector through the same transport — WITHOUT writing into v2 and without a six-hour backfill discovering it. Neither is provable by reading; both are silent when wrong.
